([[Athens, Tennessee]]) | college = [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio]] (2018–2021) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2021) * Second-team All-MAC (2020) * MAC All-Freshman Team (2019) * [[Mid-American Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|MAC Tournament]] MVP ([[2021 MAC Men's Basketball Tournament|2021]]) }} '''Jason Preston''' (born August 10, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio Bobcats]]. ==High school career== Preston played basketball for [[William R. Boone High School]] in [[Orlando, Florida]], averaging two points per game over two years.{{cite web |last1=Arkley |first1=Jason |title=Preston an unlikely freshman standout for Bobcats |url=https://www.athensmessenger.com/sports/ohiouniversity/preston-an-unlikely-freshman-standout-for-bobcats/article_fc8f8079-5695-51d0-a3e7-cc9d4a56d945.html |website=[[The Athens Messenger]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=February 25, 2019}} He stood about 6 ft (1.83 m) and weighed 140 lbs (64 kg) out of high school and applied to the [[University of Central Florida]] as a regular student, planning to major in [[journalism]]. After competing on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, Preston chose to play basketball at a prep school, joining Believe Prep Academy in [[Athens, Tennessee]].{{cite web |last1=Lopresti |first1=Mike |title=Keep an eye on Ohio's unheralded Jason Preston, an early star in college basketball 2020 |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2020-11-30/keep-eye-ohios-unheralded-jason-preston-early-star-college-basketball-2020 |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 30, 2020}} He grew four inches (10 cm) and gained experience as a [[point guard]]. Preston averaged 12 points, nine assists and seven rebounds per game, leading his team to a 31–8 record.{{cite web |title=Ohio Men's Basketball Adds Preston To 2018-19 Signing Class |url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20180515nsyuao |website=Ohio University |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=May 15, 2018}} He started out playing for the B team and was elevated to the A team after a series of strong performances, but began playing for the C team after receiving little playing time. Preston eventually managed to rejoin the A team. After posting his highlights to [[Twitter]], Preston received college basketball offers from [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio]] and [[Longwood Lancers men's basketball|Longwood]], eventually committing to play for Ohio. ==College career== As a freshman at Ohio, Preston averaged six points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, earning [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |title=Jason Preston |url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/bios/preston_jason_pbop |website=Ohio University |access-date=November 27, 2020}} On November 13, 2019, he posted a sophomore season-high 27 points, 14 rebounds and five assists in an 81–72 win over [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]].{{cite web |title=Preston scores 27 pts to lead Ohio over Iona 81-72 |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=28075038 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=November 13, 2019}} On January 21, 2020, Preston recorded 27 points, eight assists and seven rebounds in an 83–74 loss to [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]].{{cite web |last1=McMillan |first1=Lonnie |title=Jackson, Knapke lead Toledo past Ohio 83-74 |url=https://www.bobcatattack.com/basketball/story.asp?PID=1219 |website=Bobcat Attack |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=January 21, 2020}} On February 8, he scored 15 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists, becoming the second player in program history to register a triple-double, in a 77–46 win over [[Miami RedHawks men's basketball|Miami (Ohio)]].{{cite web |last1=Poisal |first1=Anthony |title=Men's Basketball: Jason Preston's pregame suggestion, triple-double carry Ohio to blowout win over Miami |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2020/02/ohio-bobcats-mens-basketball-jason-preston-battle-of-the-bricks-miami-redhawks |website=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=February 8, 2020}} As a sophomore, Preston averaged 16.8 points, 7.4 assists and 6.4 rebounds per game and was a Second Team All-MAC selection. He led the MAC and ranked second in the nation in assists.{{cite web |last1=Mauro |first1=Bryan |title=MAC Basketball: In-depth look at Ohio Bobcats junior guard Jason Preston |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/07/19/mac-basketball-in-depth-look-at-ohio-bobcats-junior-guard-jason-preston/2/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=July 19, 2020}} On November 27, 2020, Preston recorded a career-high 31 points, eight assists and six rebounds in a 77–75 loss to eighth-ranked [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Werner |first1=Jeremy |title=Quick hits: No. 8 Illini survive scare from Ohio 77-75 |url=https://247sports.com/college/illinois/Article/Illinois-basketball-Ohio-Bobcats-recap-quick-hits-155472274/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=November 27, 2020}} His story drew national attention following the performance.{{cite web |last1=Sykes II |first1=Mike D. |title=Listen to Ohio guard Jason Preston's absolutely incredible story |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/lists/jason-preston-story-ohio-illinois-guard |website=For The Win |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 28, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Colant |first1=Juliana |title=OU point guard Jason Preston goes viral over the weekend; Athens County has over 2,000 COVID-19 cases |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2020/11/ohio-university-basketball-player-jason-preston-goes-viral-covid-cases-athens-county |website=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 29, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Gaydos |first1=Ryan |title=Ohio University point guard's backstory goes viral as he drops 31 points vs. Illinois |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/ohio-university-point-guard-backstory-viral-illinois |website=[[Fox News]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 28, 2020}} On January 23, 2021, he posted his second triple-double, with 11 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds in an 85–77 win against [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]].{{cite web |title=Preston triple-double leads Ohio past Ball St. 85-77 |url=https://www.si.com/college/college-basketball/game/2307724 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=January 23, 2021}} Preston was named [[most valuable player]] of the [[2021 MAC Men's Basketball Tournament|MAC Tournament]] after leading Ohio to the title.{{cite web |last1=Kirven |first1=J. L. |title=Men's Basketball: Jason Preston and Ben Vander Plas lead Ohio back to the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2021/03/ohio-bobcats-mens-basketball-jason-preston-and-ben-vander-plas-mac-championship |website=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 14, 2021}} On March 20, in the first round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], he helped the 13th-seeded Bobcats to a 62–58 upset victory over fourth-seeded [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], recording 11 points, 13 rebounds and eight assists.{{cite web |last1=Marot |first1=Michael |title=Virginia loses 62-58 to Preston, Ohio, ending title defense |url=https://apnews.com/article/virginia-cavaliers-mens-basketball-jason-preston-coronavirus-pandemic-virginia-indiana-bb8748c06ff389599f930c676c9815b9 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 21, 2021}} As a junior, Preston averaged 15.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 7.3 assists per game, earning First Team All-MAC honors. On April 26, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball: Jason Preston declares for the 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2021/04/ohio-bobcats-mens-basketball-jason-preston-declare-for-2021-nba-draft |website=The Post |access-date=April 26, 2021 |date=April 26, 2021}} He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=Ohio Bobcats guard Jason Preston to remain in 2021 NBA draft, sign with agent |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31778557/ohio-bobcats-guard-jason-preston-remain-2021-nba-draft-sign-agent |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=July 7, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio]] | 30 || 21 || 29.5 || .434 || .208 || '''.765''' || 3.6 || 3.4 || .8 || .1 || 6.0 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio]] | '''32''' || '''32''' || '''38.1''' || '''.515''' || '''.407''' || .725 || 6.4 || '''7.4''' || 1.4 || .1 || '''16.8''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio]] | 20 || 20 || 34.6 || .514 || .390 || .596 || '''7.3''' || 7.3 || '''1.5''' || '''.3''' || 15.7 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 82 || 73 || 34.1 || .498 || .357 || .703 || 5.6 || 5.9 || 1.2 || .1 || 12.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Preston's mother, Judith Sewell, died of [[lung cancer]] when Preston was a junior in high school. His father was absent from his life. After his mother's death, Preston's aunt and uncle, who were living in [[Jamaica]], became his [[legal guardian]]s, though he remained in the United States and lived with the son of his mother's friend.
